html:
The Hopi are a Pueblo people of northeast Arizona, living in stone villages on three mesas at the south end of Black Mesa. The map spells them Hopie and shows them in 1650 and 1700.

They are dry farmers, growing maize, beans and squash in sandy fields with little rain, and their villages are very old: Oraibi has been lived in since about 1100, among the oldest towns in the United States. Their religion centres on the kachina spirits and a yearly round of ceremonies.

Spanish Franciscans built missions on the mesas in 1629. In the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 the Hopi killed the friars and tore the churches down. When Spain returned to New Mexico in the 1690s it never brought the Hopi back under rule. In 1700 the village of Awatovi let friars return, and other Hopi villages destroyed it.

Their neighbours were the Navajo, whose reservation later surrounded theirs, and the Zuni. See also Hopi on the modern map.
